title: Bram and the Garden
premise: Casper Lockridge has spent a decade hiding the gift of hearing the old god Bram's silence, working as a smuggler's guide through the Thornfell mountains while the crown's witch-hunters close in. When she shelters a fugitive child who carries the other half of Bram's broken covenant, Casper learns the god did not die—he was imprisoned by the first kings, and his fading is unraveling the boundary between realms. Hunted across the mountains by her former commander and betrayed by the smugglers who raised her, Casper must reach the buried Garden where the covenant was first sworn and choose between restoring her god or freeing him entirely. In the end she breaks the covenant rather than reforge it, giving Bram back to the world as something wilder than worship—and claiming her own name, not his mark, as the source of her belonging.
about_author: Emrys Vane is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six years leading expeditions through remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in landscapes that feel like characters, exploring what people owe to the places and powers that shaped them.

chapters.title: The Silent Bell
chapters.summary: Casper guides a cargo run through Thornfell, hiding her gift of sensing Bram's dead silence beneath mercenary pragmatism. News of the crown's gift-hunt reaches a mountain waystation, and an old client warns her to vanish. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: the uneasy comfort of a life built on staying unseen beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Child Carried
chapters.summary: Casper finds a fugitive girl, Wren, half-frozen in a ravine—marked with the same sigil Casper bears, but burning with living power instead of silence. Sheltering her means betraying every rule of survival Casper owns. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness overriding hard-won self-preservation.

chapters.title: Hollow Covenant
chapters.summary: A dying hedge-priest explains the truth: Bram was not silent but imprisoned by the first kings, split between two bearers of his mark. Wren holds the waking half; Casper holds the memory. Witch-hunters burn a village nearby. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear as destiny stops being abstract.

chapters.title: The Company of Roads
chapters.summary: Casper turns to her old smuggler network for passage, but her mentor Sella sells word of her location to buy the network's safety. Casper escapes with Wren through a collapsing pass, wounded and furious. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: grief for the found-family that chose survival over loyalty.

chapters.title: Ash and Antlers
chapters.summary: Pursued by Captain Ilsa Vey—Casper's former commander, once her closest friend—the pair take refuge among the antlered hillfolk who still keep forbidden rites. There Casper hears Bram's voice for the first time: faint, fractured, pleading. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: longing tangled with resentment toward a god who let her hide alone so long.

chapters.title: The Price of the Mark
chapters.summary: Wren learns the covenant demands one bearer's life to unbind the other; the hillfolk expect Casper, the elder mark, to be the sacrifice. Wren tries to slip away alone at night to face Vey's hunters and bargain. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt and fierce love driving a child to martyrdom.

chapters.title: Where Vey Stands
chapters.summary: Vey captures Wren but hesitates—she took the hunt only to control it from within, having lost a gifted sister to the pyres. She offers Casper a deal: surrender the child, live hidden again. Casper refuses and frees Wren, becoming a true outlaw. POV: Vey. Emotional beat: a rival revealed as a mirror, and the point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: Descent into the Garden
chapters.summary: Guided by Bram's failing voice, Casper and Wren descend through the roots of Thornfell into the buried Garden where the first kings bound their god. The realm-thin walls bleed visions of everyone Casper has failed to save. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: confronting the memory-half of herself that she has starved for a decade.

chapters.title: The Breaking
chapters.summary: In the Garden's heart, the choice appears: reforge the covenant with a life given, or shatter it and release Bram unbound—unknowable, ungoverned, possibly catastrophic. Casper refuses both offered sacrifices, breaking the covenant with her own authority as bearer. Bram rises wild and free; the mountains shake. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: defiance transmuted into faith—not in obedience, but in trust.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: The hunt collapses as Bram's awakening exposes the crown's lies; Vey stands down and testifies. Casper, no longer marked but changed, plants a seed from the Garden above ground where a shrine might grow—or might simply be a garden. She and Wren choose each other freely. POV: Casper. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—belonging claimed, not granted.
